title: 136. 1922: The Birth of the Modern World Part 1

sentences.en: On the 18th of May 1922, the British translator and novelist Sidney Schiff hosted a dinner party at the Majestic Hotel in Paris.
sentences.zh: 1922年5月18日，英国翻译家兼小说家西德尼·希夫在巴黎的杰姬尔酒店举办了一场晚宴。

sentences.en: Forty guests were invited in all, but there were four guests in particular that Schiff wanted to bring together to generate, to see sharing dinner party chat.
sentences.zh: 总共邀请了四十位宾客，其中有四位是希夫特别想聚在一起的，想看看他们聚在一起聊晚宴的样子。

sentences.en: They were Igor Stravinsky, the great Russian composer, Pablo Picasso, great cubist painter, James Joyce, Marcel Proust, probably the two greatest novelists of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 他们分别是伟大的俄国作曲家伊戈尔·斯特拉文斯基、伟大的立体主义画家巴勃罗·皮加索、詹姆斯·乔伊斯以及马塞尔·普鲁斯特——这二位大概是20世纪最伟大的两位小说家。

sentences.en: Stravinsky and Picasso turn up on time, but Joyce and Proust don't.
sentences.zh: 斯特拉文斯基和皮加索准时出现了，但乔伊斯和普鲁斯特没有。

sentences.zh: 但我觉得在德国，你确实有一种感觉。

sentences.en: So there's a guy called Volta Rathenau, who is the foreign minister, who negotiates a deal.
sentences.zh: 有个叫沃尔特·拉特瑙的人，他是外交部长，他谈判达成了一项协议。

sentences.en: He's the one who gets assassinated.
sentences.zh: 他就是那个被暗杀的人。

sentences.en: He gets assassinated, exactly, by right-wing paramilitaries.
sentences.zh: 他被暗杀了，没错，死于右翼准军事组织之手。

sentences.en: So there's a real sense of the instability at the core of the Weimar Republic.
sentences.zh: 所以魏玛共和国核心存在着一种真正的不稳定感。

sentences.en: You also have in Germany the sort of the cultural expression of the kind of the morbidity and the dissolution.
sentences.zh: 你在德国还能看到那种病态和瓦解的文化表现。

sentences.en: So you have things like the film Nosferatu.
sentences.zh: 所以你有了像电影《诺斯费拉图》这样的作品。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the, you know, which is a version of the…
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这是……的一个版本

sentences.en: Great reworking of Dracula, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 对《德古拉》的伟大重构，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly, of Dracula, a vampire story.
sentences.zh: 没错，就是《德古拉》，一个吸血鬼故事。

sentences.en: And that sort of obsession, there's a kind of vampiric obsession in German expressionist kind of cinematic culture in the 20s.
sentences.zh: 那种迷恋，在20世纪德国表现主义电影文化中有一种吸血鬼式的迷恋。

sentences.en: George Grace's cartoons are horrible.
sentences.zh: 乔治·格罗斯的漫画非常可怕。

sentences.en: Incredibly horrible, scatological scathing, yeah.
sentences.zh: 极其可怕，充满排泄物审丑和尖锐讽刺，对。

sentences.en: All of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 所有这些东西。

sentences.en: Or Fritz Lang does his first Dr. Mabuse films in 1922.
sentences.zh: 或者弗里茨·朗在1922年拍摄了他的第一部马布斯博士电影。

sentences.en: Again, sort of brooding, dark, sort of vampiric stuff.
sentences.zh: 同样是那种令人窒息、黑暗、带有吸血鬼色彩的东西。

sentences.en: So famously, in the long run, the Nazis will come to power by saying that Germany hadn't actually lost the First World War, they've stabbed in the back.
sentences.zh: 所以众所周知，从长远来看，纳粹将通过宣称德国实际上并没有输掉第一次世界大战、他们是被背后捅刀子而夺取权力。

sentences.en: So in 1922, do Germans feel that they are a defeated people or do they feel that they've been betrayed and that they could have carried on?
sentences.zh: 所以在1922年，德国人觉得自己是一个战败的民族，还是觉得他们被背叛了、其实本可以继续打下去？

sentences.en: I think it depends on the German, actually.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这取决于具体是哪个德国人。

sentences.en: I think some, you know, let's say the people that Rattenau kind of represent.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有些人，比如说，拉特瑙所代表的那类人。

sentences.en: So that would be the kind of, you know, you have a part of Germany that is invested in the Weimar Republic and they would be kind of liberal-minded, middle-class,
sentences.zh: 所以那将是那种，你知道的，德国有一部分人投资于魏玛共和国，他们将是那种思想自由、中产阶级、

sentences.en: sort of democratically-minded people.
sentences.zh: 具有民主思想的人。

sentences.en: But you have an enormous number of people in the kind of conservative, on the conservative wing of the spectrum who, you know,
sentences.zh: 但你在保守派阵营中有数量庞大的人，你知道的，

sentences.en: they don't really ever accept the legitimacy of the Weimar Republic.
sentences.zh: 他们从来不真正接受魏玛共和国的合法性。

sentences.en: They do think that Germany was betrayed in some way.
sentences.zh: 他们确实认为德国在某种程度上被背叛了。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the argument that Eric Ludendorff, former sort of co-dictator of Germany at the end of the First World War, is pushing by this point in the early 20s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是埃里希·鲁登道夫——第一次世界大战结束时德国前联合独裁者——在20岁头几年一直在推行的论点。

sentences.en: He's saying, well, we could have fought on, but the politicians wouldn't let us and we were betrayed by fifth columnists and all this sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们本可以继续战斗，但政客们不让，我们被内奸出卖了诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And obviously, the chief scapegoats are the Jews.
sentences.zh: 很明显，主要的替罪羊就是犹太人。

sentences.en: And you definitely see this already.
sentences.zh: 而且你肯定已经看到了这一点。

sentences.en: And there's a sort of paramilitary quality of German politics already.
sentences.zh: 而且德国政治已经有一种准军事化的特质。

sentences.en: So the communists fighting the right, the hard right, in Berlin and Munich and so on.
sentences.zh: 因此，共产党人在柏林、慕尼黑等地与右翼、极右翼进行战斗。

sentences.en: Presumably, the effect of that is that it's kind of delegitimizing every kind of authority, every kind of break on the resort to violence.
sentences.zh: 据推测，其结果就是它在某种程度上削弱了各种权威的合法性，削弱了对诉诸暴力的一切制约。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think violence, a kind of paramilitary violence is built into, is implicit in the sort of post-war Germany from the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为暴力，一种准军事化的暴力，从一开始就内置于战后德国之中，是隐含在其中的。

sentences.en: Because its early months are scarred by so much fighting, kind of attempt to set up a Soviet in Munich and so on, kind of Bavarian Socialist Republic,
sentences.zh: 因为它的头几个月饱受冲突折磨，比如试图在慕尼黑建立苏维埃等等，某种巴伐利亚苏维埃共和国，

sentences.en: endless sort of putches and coups and so on.
sentences.zh: 没完没了的暴动、政变等等。

sentences.en: And this sort of sense of that the Weimar, that the Republic never has, it never really commands widespread acceptance across German society.
sentences.zh: 而且魏玛、共和国从来没有、也从未真正赢得德国社会广泛认可的这种感觉。

sentences.en: And I think that that means that although it later on in the 20s, there has this brief period where it seems like it's becoming a bit more stable.
sentences.zh: 我认为这意味着，尽管在20世纪20年代后期，它经历了一个短暂的时期，看起来似乎变得更加稳定了一些。

sentences.en: So that's after the great inflation of 1922 to 1933 has abated.
sentences.zh: 也就是在1922至1933年的恶性通货膨胀消退之后。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the inflation.
sentences.zh: 所以是通货膨胀。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the inflation is absolutely crazy.
sentences.zh: 而且通货膨胀简直疯狂。

sentences.en: That's the key.
sentences.zh: 这就是关键。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the real killer.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这才是真正的杀手锏。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the inflation, I think at the beginning of 22, a mark is worth, you can get something like 350 marks to the dollar.
sentences.zh: 所以通货膨胀，我认为在22年年初，一马克的值是，你用一美元可以换到大约350马克。

sentences.en: And by the end of 1922, it's something like, I mean, it sounds unbelievable, 7,400 marks to the dollar.
sentences.zh: 到了1922年底，大约是，我的意思是，这听起来令人难以置信，一美元可以换到7400马克。

sentences.en: So that's, I mean, a colossal change, a colossal sort of debauching of your currency.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着，一场巨大的变革，你本国货币的一场灾难性的贬值。

sentences.en: And then by late 1923, it's billions of marks to the dollar.
sentences.zh: 然后到了1923年晚期，一美元可以换到几十亿马克。

sentences.en: So, I mean, that's your classic image of the wheelbarrows for the banknotes.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这就是用独轮车运送钞票的经典画面。

sentences.en: And obviously that destroys people's savings.
sentences.zh: 显然，这摧毁了人们的积蓄。

sentences.en: It erodes middle-class people's faith in the system.
sentences.zh: 它侵蚀了中产阶级对体制的信任。

sentences.en: And it pulporises the middle classes.
sentences.zh: 而且它将中产阶级粉碎了。

sentences.en: Yeah, completely.
sentences.zh: 是的，彻底粉碎。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: And a pulporised middle class is always the wellspring of revolutionary activity.
sentences.zh: 一个被粉碎的中产阶级永远是革命活动的源泉。

sentences.en: And don't forget that all this is happening, Tom, against the backdrop of what we're going to talk about in a few minutes, which is Bolshevism,
sentences.zh: 而且别忘了，汤姆，这一切都发生在我们将要在几分钟后谈论的背景之下，也就是布尔什维主义，

sentences.en: which is the arrival of the Russian Revolution.
sentences.zh: 也就是俄国革命的到来。

sentences.en: I think.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But Dominic, just on the topic.
sentences.zh: 但是多米尼克，就这个话题而言。

sentences.en: So we're looking at 1922 as, you know, the year that modernity begins.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将1922年视为，你知道的，现代性开端之年。

sentences.en: One of the enduring effects of the great inflation in Germany is a German horror at inflation.
sentences.zh: 德国大通胀带来的持久影响之一，就是德国人对通货膨胀的恐惧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which has been a massive, massive factor in the evolution of the European Union.
sentences.zh: 这在欧盟的发展过程中一直是一个极其巨大的因素。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So in that sense, the economics of Germany in 1922 continue to reverberate right the way up into the present day.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，1922年德国的经济状况一直持续影响到今天。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think they do, because, of course,
sentences.zh: 是的，我想确实如此，因为当然，

sentences.en: the German response to the Eurozone crisis was partly informed by the fact that generations of German politicians have always sort of said never again.
sentences.zh: 德国对欧元区危机的反应，部分原因在于几代德国政客总是抱着“绝不再发生”的心态。

sentences.en: You know, inflation is the great enemy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，通货膨胀是头号大敌。

sentences.en: Which is ironic, because, actually, the thing that really brought the Nazis to power was not the inflation.
sentences.zh: 这很讽刺，因为实际上，真正把纳粹推上台的不是通货膨胀。

sentences.en: It was the unemployment caused by the onset of the Great Depression after 1931.
sentences.zh: 而是1931年后大萧条爆发所导致的失业率。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's the inflation, oddly, that has become the defining image of Weimar Germany, of its failure to come to secure order.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，奇怪的是，通货膨胀成了魏玛德国及其未能建立稳定秩序的代名词。

sentences.en: Well, I suppose Germany was so rich and prosperous and successful before the war that the, you know, impoverished bourgeois carrying mark notes on wheel barriers.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想德国在战前是如此富有、繁荣和成功，以至于那些，你知道的，推着独轮车带着马克纸币的穷困潦倒的资产阶级。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, you know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的。

sentences.en: Well, I think, actually, what you get is, I don't know if you've read that book,
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上，我认为你会发现，我不知道你是否读过那本书，

sentences.en: but Sir Colm Tobin had a book last year about Thomas Mann and a novel about the life of Thomas Mann.
sentences.zh: 科尔姆·托宾爵士去年出了一本关于托马斯·曼的书，一本关于托马斯·曼生平的小说。

sentences.en: And Sir Thomas Mann wrote the great book about kind of bourgeois German Victorianism, Buddenbrooks, about this family in Lübeck.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·曼爵士写过那部关于资产阶级德国维多利亚风格的伟大著作《布登勃洛克家族》，讲述了吕贝克的一个家族。

sentences.en: And when you read the Colm Tobin book about Mann's life, just that journey that nobody really in the English-speaking world can possibly contemplate, that you go from pre-war,
sentences.zh: 当你阅读科尔姆·托宾关于曼生平的书时，就会发现英语世界里没有人能够真正想象的那段历程，你从战前，

sentences.en: you know, Germany, the most dynamic, the most sort of self-satisfied, prosperous country in Europe.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，德国，欧洲最具活力、最自我满足、最繁荣的国家。

sentences.en: And in many ways the most progressive.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面也是最进步的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in many ways, and very progressive to this basket case in the 1920s and then the horrors of the 30s and 40s and so on.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，而且非常进步，变成了20世纪20年代的这个烂摊子，然后又是30和40年代等等的恐怖。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just the most extraordinary trajectory.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直是最非凡的轨迹。

sentences.en: And so if we're talking about the horrors of the 1930s and 40s, and indeed the horrors of the 20th century generally, the fact that, so 1922 is a key year in,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们谈论30年代和40年代的恐怖，以及整个20世纪的恐怖，事实上，1922年是一个关键年份，

sentences.en: so it's establishment of the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 也就是苏联的建立。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's effectively the establishment of Stalin's primacy, because although Lenin is still alive, he's had the stroke.
sentences.zh: 而且这实际上也是斯大林确立最高地位的开始，因为尽管列宁还活着，但他已经中风了。

sentences.en: And Stalin has made himself general secretary of the Communist Party, and he uses this as a way to essentially muscle out the opposition and bring Lenin under his thumb.
sentences.zh: 斯大林让自己担任了共产党总书记，并以此为手段基本上排挤了反对派，将列宁置于自己的掌控之下。

sentences.en: So communism, obviously, is a massive theme for the decades that are to come, but also in 1922, and we did an episode on the Rubicon a little bit earlier this week.
sentences.zh: 所以共产主义显然是未来几十年的一个巨大主题，但在1922年，本周早些时候我们在《卢比孔河》中做过一期节目。

sentences.en: But you have Mussolini's march on Rome, and so the rise of fascism.
sentences.zh: 但你看到了墨索里尼的进军罗马，以及法西斯的崛起。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And I think those two things are completely intertwined.
sentences.zh: 我认为这两件事是完全交织在一起的。

sentences.en: So what happens in Italy?
sentences.zh: 那么意大利发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, maybe we'll come on to Russia in just a second.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许我们一会儿再谈俄罗斯。

sentences.en: And so Italy, Italy had entered the First World War very foolishly, in my view, to try and get more territory.
sentences.zh: 所以意大利，在我看来，意大利非常愚蠢地加入了第一次世界大战，试图获取更多领土。

sentences.en: It had basically changed sides, done a dirty deal to come in on the Allied side because they wanted to snatch bits of the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是背叛了阵营，为了抢夺奥匈帝国的领土而与盟军做了肮脏的交易加入了进来。

sentences.en: The Italian army had performed incredibly poorly, soldiers very heroically, but the generals utterly inept.
sentences.zh: 意大利军队表现极其糟糕，士兵们非常英勇，但将军们却极其无能。

sentences.en: They'd lost 700,000 men.
sentences.zh: 他们损失了70万士兵。

sentences.en: They'd run up colossal debts.
sentences.zh: 他们背负了巨额债务。

sentences.en: They'd gained virtually nothing.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎一无所获。

sentences.en: And at the end of the war, as they see it, they're fobbed off by the other allies.
sentences.zh: 在战争结束时，在他们看来，他们被其他盟友愚弄了。

sentences.en: They're not given the great empire they want in the Adriatic.
sentences.zh: 他们没有得到他们在亚得里亚海梦寐以求的伟大帝国。

sentences.en: They're given a bit of territory, but nothing like what they think they're going to get.
sentences.zh: 他们得到了一点领土，但跟他们想象的完全没法比。

sentences.en: And there's this tremendous sense in Italy that they have been utterly shortchanged, that they've had this horrendous experience.
sentences.zh: 意大利有一种强烈的被严重剥削的感觉，觉得他们经历了这场可怕的经历。

sentences.en: I mean, the fighting, the Italian front.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，战斗，意大利前线。

sentences.en: They're kind of blowing off the tops of mountains, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 他们简直是把山顶都炸飞了，对吧？

sentences.en: It's awful.
sentences.zh: 这太可怕了。

sentences.en: It's absolutely awful.
sentences.zh: 这绝对太可怕了。

sentences.en: They fight, there's the Battle of the Isonzo.
sentences.zh: 他们在战斗，发生了伊松佐河战役。

sentences.en: There were 12 battles of the Isonzo, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想伊松佐河战役一共进行了12次。

sentences.en: They're just constantly charging at the Austrians and just being machine gunned.
sentences.zh: 他们就是不断地向奥地利人冲锋，然后被机枪扫射。

sentences.en: So some of all, I went to Lake Como, which I'd never been to, and climbed up a mountain.
sentences.zh: 所以，我去过科莫湖，我以前从未去过那里，还爬上了一座山。

sentences.en: And there was this tunnel that kind of went through, I mean, went through a mountain that had been cut, you know, hacked out with handpicks.
sentences.zh: 那里有一条穿山隧道，我的意思是，那是一条穿过一座山的隧道，是用手镐凿出来的。

sentences.en: And you just saw the absolute waste of effort that went into all that.
sentences.zh: 你一眼就能看出这一切背后所付出的绝对是徒劳的努力。

sentences.en: But the Italian front is so horrible that there are all these stories of Italians charging up their caste,
sentences.zh: 但意大利前线是如此可怕，以至于流传着各种关于意大利人冲向喀斯特山脉的故事，

sentences.en: which is this sort of exposed limestone mountainous region in the sort of Italian-Slovenian border.
sentences.zh: 这是意大利与斯洛文尼亚边境附近的一个暴露的石灰岩山区。

sentences.en: There are all these stories of Italians charging up these hillsides.
sentences.zh: 到处都是关于意大利人冲上这些山坡的故事。

sentences.en: And the Austrians at the top of the hill shouting at them to go back.
sentences.zh: 山顶的奥地利人大声叫他们回去。

sentences.en: They're basically saying, if you turn back and run away, we won't shoot at you because, you know, we're going to kill you.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上在说，如果你转头逃跑，我们不会向你开枪，因为，你知道的，我们要杀了你。

sentences.en: And the Italians just keep coming and the Austrians just mow them down.
sentences.zh: 而意大利人源源不断地冲上来，奥地利人只是把他们无情地割倒。

sentences.en: And the Austrian army is completely inept itself.
sentences.zh: 而且奥地利军队本身也完全无能。

sentences.en: So the fact that it's able to hold off the Italians tells you how badly the Italian generals are performing.
sentences.zh: 所以它能够抵挡住意大利人这一事实，说明了意大利将军们的表现有多么糟糕。

sentences.en: Anyway, this is a bit of a segue, a bit of a sidetrack, rather.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，这有点像个过渡，或者说是一个题外话。

sentences.en: But Italy is in a terrible state at the end of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 但一战结束时的意大利处于一种可怕的状态。

sentences.en: It's absolutely in the early 20s.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪20年代初，它绝对是这样的。

sentences.en: It is riven by labor unreSt.
sentences.zh: 它被劳资冲突搞得支离破碎。

sentences.en: There are whole waves of factory occupations.
sentences.zh: 到处都是工厂占领浪潮。

sentences.en: There's tremendous unemployment.
sentences.zh: 失业率极高。

sentences.en: There's great hostility, sort of class hostility and so on.
sentences.zh: 存在着巨大的敌意，阶级敌意等等。

sentences.en: And what you have in by 1922 is that this guy who has been a socialist journalist, Mussolini, completely shamelessly basically changes his colors and offers his support.
sentences.zh: 到了1922年，这个曾担任社会主义记者、毫无廉耻地改变立场的家伙墨索里尼，开始提供他的支持。

sentences.en: And basically, all the radical energy that he had previously put into the left wing sort of cause, he basically gets into bed with the landowners,
sentences.zh: 基本上，他以前投入到左翼事业中的所有激进能量，现在却与地主、

sentences.en: factory owners and the right and says, you know, my squadristi, my squads, my kind of paramilitary units are at your disposal to fight off Bolshevism.
sentences.zh: 工厂主和右翼同流合污，说，你知道的，我的突击队，我的准军事部队听候你们差遣，用来抵抗布尔什维主义。

sentences.en: And there's a series of punch ups and there's a real sense of kind of seething violence.
sentences.zh: 发生了一系列冲突，有一种真正的暗流涌动的暴力感。

sentences.en: And then there's a general strike and there's some of the fails.
sentences.zh: 然后爆发了总罢工，有些失败了。

sentences.en: And against that backdrop, Mussolini launches his famous march on Rome.
sentences.zh: 在这种背景下，墨索里尼发起了他著名的进军罗马。

sentences.en: Which isn't really a march, is it?
sentences.zh: 这其实根本算不上进军，对吧？

sentences.en: No, it's an absolute con.
sentences.zh: 不，这完全是一场骗局。

sentences.en: It's a complete con.
sentences.zh: 这完全是一场骗局。

sentences.en: He gets up in Naples and sort of gives this tremendous speech saying, we should all march on Rome and seize Paris.
sentences.zh: 他在那不勒斯发表了一场声势浩大的演讲，说我们应该全部进军罗马并占领巴黎。

sentences.en: Our program is simple.
sentences.zh: 我们的纲领很简单。

sentences.en: We want to rule Italy.
sentences.zh: 我们要统治意大利。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But then he doesn't go himself.
sentences.zh: 但他自己却没有去。

sentences.en: He's such a coward.
sentences.zh: 他是个十足的懦夫。

sentences.en: He doesn't go.
sentences.zh: 他没有去。

sentences.en: He goes off to Milan instead.
sentences.zh: 相反，他跑去了米兰。

sentences.en: Well, they all, he says, you, you, you, you and you, you can lead the march.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们所有人，他说，你、你、你、你还有你，你们可以领导进军。

sentences.en: I'll just weigh in.
sentences.zh: 我随后就到。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then the king, the king makes him, appoints him prime minister.
sentences.zh: 然后国王，国王让他当上了首相，任命他为首相。

sentences.en: So the king, it's a really interesting parallel with what happens in Germany in 19, you know, the end of 32, early 33.
sentences.zh: 所以国王，这与1932年底到1933年初德国发生的事情有着非常有趣的相似之处。

sentences.en: Um, the Italian prime minister is a guy called Luigi Factor.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当时的意大利首相是一个叫路易吉·法克塔的人。

sentences.en: And he basically says, you know, these fascists are a rabble.
sentences.zh: 他基本上说，你知道的，这些法西斯分子只是一群乌合之众。

sentences.en: There's 20,000 of them.
sentences.zh: 他们有两万人。

sentences.en: They're pouring with rain.
sentences.zh: 下着倾盆大雨。

sentences.en: They're very bedraggled.
sentences.zh: 他们狼狈不堪。

sentences.en: We don't have anything to fear from them.
sentences.zh: 我们没有什么好怕他们的。

sentences.en: I've got more troops.
sentences.zh: 我有更多的军队。

sentences.en: I'll declare a state of emergency, crush them, you know, and that'll be fine.
sentences.zh: 我要宣布进入紧急状态，粉碎他们，你知道的，这就没事了。

sentences.en: And the king panics and refuses to sign the order of Victor Emmanuel the third.
sentences.zh: 结果维托里奥·埃马努埃莱三世国王惊慌失措，拒绝签署命令。

sentences.en: And he says, he thinks, no, maybe the thing to do is, because he's obviously quite conservative himself.
sentences.zh: 他认为，不，也许该做的是，因为他自己显然也相当保守。

sentences.en: He thinks maybe the thing to do is bring Mussolini on side, you know, and let's not have any trouble.
sentences.zh: 他认为也许该做的是把墨索里尼拉拢过来，你知道的，别惹麻烦。

sentences.en: And he appoints Mussolini as prime minister.
sentences.zh: 于是他任命墨索里尼为首相。

sentences.en: And Mussolini turns up for the, for the ceremony in his black shirt and the top hat.
sentences.zh: 墨索里尼穿着他的黑衫军服和高顶礼帽出席了典礼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, Dan Jackson has been on our podcast to talk about the birth of the railways and the top hat, but he wasn't wearing a black shirt.
sentences.zh: 丹·杰克逊曾做客我们的播客谈论铁路的诞生和高顶礼帽，但他当时没穿黑衬衫。

sentences.en: No, he wasn't.
sentences.zh: 不，他没穿。

sentences.en: Well, he also wasn't about to become prime minister of Italy, to be fair to Dan.
sentences.zh: 而且，说句公道话，他当时也没有要成为意大利首相的意思。

sentences.en: No, he wasn't.
sentences.zh: 不，他没有。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: So, obviously, the rise of fascism in Italy.
sentences.zh: 所以，显然，法西斯主义在意大利的崛起。

sentences.en: I mean, if you're looking at 1922, that's an absolutely massive moment, because then people start in Germany saying, where is our Mussolini?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你看看1922年，那是一个绝对重大的时刻，因为随后德国人开始问，我们的墨索里尼在哪里？

sentences.en: Well, but Dominic, you said, so Mussolini goes from being a socialist to being a fasciSt.
sentences.zh: 但是，多米尼克，你刚才说，墨索里尼从一个社会主义者变成了法西斯分子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that this was a total reversal.
sentences.zh: 而这是一个彻底的转变。

sentences.en: But in a way, in a way, I mean, he's not becoming a kind of supporter of liberal economics or capitalism.
sentences.zh: 但从某种意义上说，我是说，他并没有成为那种支持自由经济或资本主义的人。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: Adam Smith or something.
sentences.zh: 亚当·斯密或者类似的人。

sentences.en: I mean, essentially, the energies of the fascists and the communists, they're so electrifying because they're so similar.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从本质上讲，法西斯分子和共产主义者的能量之所以如此具有煽动性，是因为它们太相似了。

sentences.en: Isn't that right?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, you're right.
sentences.zh: 对，你说得对。

sentences.en: I mean, we could get into a huge conversation here, couldn't we, about the sort of the protean and the sort of, yeah, the ambiguity.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们可以在这里展开一场宏大的对话，关于那种多面性，还有那种，对，那种模糊性。

sentences.en: Because they're national socialists.
sentences.zh: 因为他们是国家社会主义者。

sentences.en: Yeah, the ambiguity of fascism in the early 20s, that it appears both radical and conservative.
sentences.zh: 对，20年代初法西斯主义的模糊性，它表现得既激进又保守。

sentences.en: Of course, it appears both modern and anti-modern.
sentences.zh: 当然，它表现得既现代又反现代。

sentences.en: So, fascist parties classically use radio, cars, planes.
sentences.zh: 所以，法西斯政党通常会使用收音机、汽车、飞机。

sentences.en: They glory in their modernity at the same time as they're harking back to an idealized, yeah, to an idealized paSt.
sentences.zh: 他们在陶醉于现代性的同时，又在怀念一个理想化的，对，一个理想化的过去。

sentences.en: And the guy who blazes the trail for that for Mussolini is Denunzio.
sentences.zh: 而为墨索里尼开辟这条道路的人是邓南遮。

sentences.en: Terrible man.
sentences.zh: 可怕的人。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Basically, the man who got Italy into the First World War in the first place.
sentences.zh: 基本上，正是这个人把意大利拉入了第一次世界大战。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And he establishes a kind of proto-fascist state in Trieste, which is where Joyce had been.
sentences.zh: 他在的里雅斯特建立了一种准法西斯国家，乔伊斯曾去过那里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And of course, Denunzio is another poet.
sentences.zh: 而且当然，邓南遮也是一位诗人。

sentences.en: Another poet.
sentences.zh: 又一位诗人。

sentences.en: Yeah, like Enid Blyton.
sentences.zh: 对，就像伊妮德·布莱顿。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, anyway, so that's enough about fascists.
sentences.zh: 总之，关于法西斯就说这么多了。

sentences.en: What about communists?
sentences.zh: 那共产主义者呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think, you see, I think, I don't know what you think, Tom.
sentences.zh: 对，我想，你看，我想，我不知道你怎么想，汤姆。

sentences.en: I think the two keys to this whole period of the Great War and communism, because it's fear of communism that drives a lot of the sort of right-wing stuff.
sentences.zh: 我认为理解整个第一次世界大战和共产主义时期的两个关键在于，因为正是对共产主义的恐惧驱动了大量右翼言论。

sentences.en: Not that the right-wing stuff doesn't have roots of its own, but I think that paralyzing fear of Bolshevism.
sentences.zh: 并不是说右翼言论没有它自己的根源，但我认为那种对布尔什维克主义的麻痹性恐惧……

sentences.en: I mean, paralyzing is the wrong word, actually.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，“麻痹性”这个词其实用错了。

sentences.en: It's an energizing fear of communism.
sentences.zh: 那是一种激发潜能的对共产主义的恐惧。

sentences.en: So Russia, it's had its revolutions.
sentences.zh: 所以俄罗斯，它经历了革命。

sentences.en: It's been through this period sort of from 1918 to 1920 of civil war, of this incredibly weird civil war with lots of different people, and the Czechs are involved,
sentences.zh: 它在1918年到1920年期间经历了一场内战，这场极其诡异的内战有许多不同的人参与，捷克人也卷进去了，

sentences.en: and the Allies are sending troops.
sentences.zh: 协约国也派出了军队。

sentences.en: Most of the sort of the civil war is done and dusted by 1920, but they're still mopping up in Central Asia in 1922.
sentences.zh: 内战的大部分内容在1920年就已经尘埃落定，但他们在1922年仍在清理中亚的残余势力。

sentences.en: And, in fact, extraordinarily, the last Allied forces, so the last Japanese forces, don't leave Siberia until 1922.
sentences.zh: 事实上，不可思议的是，最后一批协约国军队，也就是最后一批日本军队，直到1922年才离开西伯利亚。

sentences.en: They're in Vladivostok, and they leave in the summer, and then the Red Army marches into Vladivostok on the 25th of October.
sentences.zh: 他们在符拉迪沃斯托克，于夏天离开，然后红军在10月25日开进符拉迪沃斯托克。

sentences.en: But what's also going on, which I hadn't really appreciated until reading up on this,
sentences.zh: 但还有一件事正在发生，在我阅读相关资料之前我并没有真正意识到，

sentences.en: was that there's a lot of attention given to the sort of famine caused by Stalin's collectivization measures later on.
sentences.zh: 那就是人们把很多注意力放在了后来斯大林农业集体化措施所造成的大饥荒上。

sentences.en: But there's a tremendously horrendous famine in Russia itself in 1922.
sentences.zh: 但在1922年的俄罗斯本土，发生了一场极其惨烈的大饥荒。

sentences.en: So about 5 million people probably die of starvation.
sentences.zh: 所以大概有500万人死于饥饿。

sentences.en: God, that's incredible, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 天哪，这太难以置信了，对吧？

sentences.en: You don't even…
sentences.zh: 你甚至不……

sentences.en: On the Volga.
sentences.zh: 在伏尔加河一带。

sentences.en: And that barely even registers.
sentences.zh: 而这几乎没有引起什么关注。

sentences.en: In places like Kazan and Samara.
sentences.zh: 在喀山和萨马拉这样的大城市。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: That now, so much has happened that there are only 5 million people that that's kind of loSt.
sentences.zh: 现在，发生了太多事情，以至于只有500万人死亡这件事似乎被遗忘了。

sentences.en: While the Spanish flu is also…
sentences.zh: 而西班牙流感也同时……

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: Spanish flu is kind of becoming…
sentences.zh: 西班牙流感正变得……

sentences.en: Well, I suppose…
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想……

sentences.en: Well, okay, but you've had the First World War, millions die.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧，但你经历了第一次世界大战，数百万人死亡。

sentences.en: Spanish flu, millions die.
sentences.zh: 西班牙流感，数百万人死亡。

sentences.en: This famine, which I'd never even heard of.
sentences.zh: 还有这场我甚至从未听说过的饥荒。

sentences.en: Yeah, millions.
sentences.zh: 对，数百万人。

sentences.en: I heard the one in Ukraine, but I hadn't heard this one.
sentences.zh: 我听说过乌克兰的那场，但没听说过这一场。

sentences.en: Something like 10 million people have died in the Russian Civil War.
sentences.zh: 大约有1000万人在俄国内战中丧生。

sentences.en: I mean, colossal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，庞大得惊人。

sentences.en: I mean, just unbelievable figures.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些数字简直令人难以置信。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, and it's like Hitler says, when you start talking about millions, the brain fades.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，就像希特勒说的，当你开始谈论数百万时，大脑就麻木了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You tune out.
sentences.zh: 你就不去想了。

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely what happens.
sentences.zh: 我想这绝对是人之常情。

sentences.en: So there's been a sort of…
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一种……

sentences.en: The loss of one life is a tragedy.
sentences.zh: 死一个人是一场悲剧。

sentences.en: Yeah, and a million is a statistic, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，而死一百万只是一个统计数字，完全如此。

sentences.en: But the Soviet Union is…
sentences.zh: 但苏联是……

sentences.en: Well, it's not yet the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它还不是苏联。

sentences.en: Russia is in a very uncertain place because they've had what they called war communism, where they basically seized estates and they tried to suppress all capitalism.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯处在一个非常不确定的状态，因为他们实行了所谓的战时共产主义，他们基本上没收了庄园，并试图压制所有资本主义。

sentences.en: Then in 1921, Lenin had slightly changed course.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1921年，列宁稍微改变了方向。

sentences.en: And he had said, well, we'll allow some small enterprise to happen and peasants can sell their surpluses.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，我们将允许一些小型企业存在，农民可以出售他们的剩余产品。

sentences.en: And this is what it's called is new economic policy, NEP.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的新经济政策，简称NEP。

sentences.en: But then, as you say, Lenin has this stroke in May 1922.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，列宁在1922年5月突然中风了。

sentences.en: And it's a great what-if, actually, Tom.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这是一个巨大的“如果”，汤姆。

sentences.en: I mean, it's the great what-ifs that Trotskyists and Stalinists have argued about for decades.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是托洛茨基主义者和斯大林主义者争论了几十年的巨大假设。

sentences.en: What would have happened if Lenin…
sentences.zh: 如果列宁……会发生什么？

sentences.en: What did Lenin really want for Russia?
sentences.zh: 列宁对俄罗斯真正的期望是什么？

sentences.en: Lenin has this stroke.
sentences.zh: 列宁中风了。

sentences.en: And as you said, Stalin, he really begins his rise.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，斯大林确实开始了权力崛起。

sentences.en: He gets…
sentences.zh: 他得到了……

sentences.en: He controls Lenin.
sentences.zh: 他控制了列宁。

sentences.en: He controls access to Lenin.
sentences.zh: 他控制了接触列宁的渠道。

sentences.en: He's general secretary of the party.
sentences.zh: 他是党的总书记。

sentences.en: So he's sharing power with two other guys, particularly Kamenev and Zinoviev.
sentences.zh: 所以他与另外两个人分享权力，特别是加米涅夫和季诺维也夫。

sentences.en: But there is this sort of sense that Stalin is…
sentences.zh: 但有一种感觉，斯大林正在……

sentences.en: Because he has the party machine, he is the coming man.
sentences.zh: 因为他掌握了党内机器，他成了当红人物。

sentences.en: And it's Stalin who is probably the key player in the creation of the USSR.
sentences.zh: 而且斯大林可能是创建苏联的关键人物。

sentences.en: Which is announced in December, is it?
sentences.zh: 是在12月宣布的，对吧？

sentences.en: December, exactly.
sentences.zh: 12月，确切地说。

sentences.en: They have the big meetings to decide it.
sentences.zh: 他们召开了重要会议来决定此事。

sentences.en: So 28th to 30th of December.
sentences.zh: 也就是12月28日到30日。

sentences.en: And it's not quite what Lenin wanted.
sentences.zh: 这并不完全是列宁想要的。

sentences.en: So Lenin had wanted a union of Soviet republics of Europe and Asia.
sentences.zh: 所以列宁原本希望建立一个欧洲和亚洲苏维埃共和国联盟。

sentences.en: And Stalin changed the title to the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics.
sentences.zh: 而斯大林把名称改成了苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟。

sentences.en: I think partly because Lenin wanted…
sentences.zh: 我想部分是因为列宁希望……

sentences.en: Lenin seems to have wanted a slightly more kind of federal system.
sentences.zh: 列宁似乎想要一个稍微偏向联邦制的系统。

sentences.en: He hated the idea of Russian…
sentences.zh: 他痛恨俄罗斯的……

sentences.en: Great Russian chauvinism.
sentences.zh: 大俄罗斯沙文主义。

sentences.en: Liberal.
sentences.zh: 自由主义。

sentences.en: And Stalin, sort of paradoxically, despite the fact he was Georgian, was not so keen on that.
sentences.zh: 而斯大林，有点矛盾的是，尽管他是格鲁吉亚人，却不太喜欢那样。

sentences.en: He didn't want to encourage nationalism.
sentences.zh: 他不想助长民族主义。

sentences.en: So they take out the Europe and Asia stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以他们去掉了欧洲和亚洲的字眼。

sentences.en: And it's just the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics.
sentences.zh: 这就成了苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟。

sentences.en: And it ends up…
sentences.zh: 最后它……

sentences.en: You know, it basically covers the old Tsarist Empire.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它基本上涵盖了旧沙皇帝国。

sentences.en: But isn't it also that Lenin was, you know, in the best Marxist sense, wanted a universal revolution?
sentences.zh: 但难道不是因为列宁，你知道的，用最纯正的马克思主义意义来说，想要一场世界革命吗？

sentences.en: And it's Stalin in the long run who will go for socialism…
sentences.zh: 而从长远来看，斯大林将致力于实现社会主义……

sentences.en: Socialism in one country.
sentences.zh: 一国社会主义。

sentences.en: In one country.
sentences.zh: 在一国内建成社会主义。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly right.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: So you're starting to see the process by which the Soviet Union, as it becomes in December,
sentences.zh: 所以你开始看到这样一个进程：苏联在12月正式诞生后，

sentences.en: will essentially become a communist equivalent of the Tsarist Empire.
sentences.zh: 本质上将成为沙皇帝国的共产主义替代版。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right, actually, Tom.
sentences.zh: 对，我想确实如此，汤姆。
